title: Ridgeline Consumer Credit Account Standing: Suspension, Reinstatement and Charge-Off
content:
Ridgeline Consumer Credit account standing follows the delinquency recorded on statements and is changed only by the system.

| Standing change | When it happens |
|---|---|
| Active to suspended | a statement shows days past due at or above the tier's suspension threshold; no new purchases or draws are authorized while the account is suspended |
| Suspended to active (reinstated) | the latest statement shows a past-due amount of 0.00 and the on-time streak is at least the tier's reinstatement count |
| Suspended to charged off | a statement shows days past due at or above the tier's charge-off threshold |

**On-time streak.** Counted over the statements issued after the most recent statement whose past-due amount was above zero: the number of consecutive statements, counted back from the latest, whose minimum payment due was covered by payments credited on or before their due date.

**Limits of servicing.** Ridgeline Customer Care cannot reinstate an account early, reverse a suspension or reverse a charge-off. A payment toward a charged-off balance is accepted but does not reopen the account.

## Hypothetical streak

Statements (oldest to latest): March past-due 45.00; April minimum covered on time; May minimum covered on time; June minimum covered on time, past-due 0.00. The streak counts April, May and June: 3. With a reinstatement count of 2 or 3 the suspended account is reinstated on the June statement. Had May's minimum been covered only after its due date, the streak counted back from June would be 1.

## Hypothetical thresholds

With a 60-day suspension threshold, a statement showing 59 days past due leaves an active account active, and one showing 60 suspends it.
